story: When I was 10 years old, my class held an event to help us discover our best-suited careers. The method? A highly comprehensive, 10 question, five-minute survey. It was foolproof. Within half an hour of completing the survey, we were called up to the front of the room, one by one, to collect an envelope with our name on it. Naturally, my name was called last.

As I made my way to the front, my classmates buzzed with excitement, boasting about their impressive career assignments: "leader," "warrior," "builder." I finally reached my now lone envelope, and returned to my seat, heart racing. Inside this envelope, I thought, lay my destiny.
I took a deep breath, bracing for greatness, and ripped into it. There, staring back at me in bold letters, was a single word: helper.
I was crushed. Helper? Helper?! How? It felt so plain, so unremarkable. This is my fate? Why couldn’t I have been destined for more?

Now, as an adult, a manager, and a creative, I realize that envelope was the golden ticket and I was Charlie. It wasn’t just a word, it was the truth. Helping others is my calling. Whether it’s supporting my teams or helping my clients make an impact, I’ve learned that being a helper is far from ordinary, it’s extraordinary.
